takeaways.text: GCC banks deploy AI across customer-facing and operational domains: Emirates NBD launched travel assistant and contact centre platform reducing processing times 30%, while Riyad Bank deployed HR, fraud detection and trade finance automation.

Bahrain banks advancing AI governance and certification: Al Salam Bank achieved first regional ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management system certification, while NBB and BBK launched AI initiatives with structured programmes and partnerships.

Qatar Islamic Bank deployed AI across retail, corporate and risk domains: customer behaviour analysis in mobile apps, corporate banking process streamlining, fraud management system and RegTech automation.

External partnerships accelerating AI adoption: Emirates NBD partnered with Techstars for AI testing across compliance and risk management; Al Rajhi Bank leveraged Ejada Systems for digital transformation.
Riyad Bank achieved measurable AI results: trade finance document automation drove 19% growth in letters of credit issuance; ATM cash forecast model reduced operational costs and carbon footprint.
GCC banks are deploying AI across customer-facing and operational domains: travel assistants, banking robots, ecosystem partnerships, and formal AI governance frameworks.
Al Salam Bank achieved ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management system certification, becoming the first bank in the region with formal AI governance certification.
Qatar Islamic Bank won top AI awards from Global Finance for the Middle East, while JPMorgan ranked first globally for AI maturity in banking for consecutive years.
Central banks and regulators warn of systemic risks from rapid AI adoption: macroeconomic exposure from concentrated AI investments, potential market shocks, and risk management gaps.
Over 90% of European banks already use AI, and agentic AI is being scaled in partnerships like Infosys and ABN AMRO, while a major Norwegian bank automated operations replacing over 400 staff.
